During Adam's drawing session today on Twitch, he and Christopher answered questions for the group, ranging from the newly announced OblivAeon expansion to the mysterious Parse promo card. I have copied as many of the questions from the 2+ hour conversation as I could, and edited many of the topics that fit together. We also were able to watch the excellent drawings of the Harpy and a promo Parse! Overall, great introduction to the upcoming OblivAeon. Enjoy!

 

 

Edit: A few things of note:

- You can watch the feed from today on http://www.twitch.tv/greaterthangames/profile. There is no audio, but awesome to watch.

- There will be 5 heroes, the number of environments "depends on you", and the number of villains is "hard to define"

- Notes on Con, Parse, alternate reality heroes, and the ARG.

posts.cooked:
Christopher mentioned that you cannot defeat OblivAeon until you figure out how to do so. I know that the whole Legacy thing has been kind of a buzz word lately in the gaming world, but I think it would be really cool to "unlock" certain hidden packets in the game based on what you've done so far in your plays, a la Risk Legacy. Could you just tear into all of the envelopes straight out the gate? Of course, but where would be the fun in that! 

Examples for those who don't know Legacy games would be along the lines of: Open this packet when you defeat your second Scion; or, Open this packet after your first loss; or, Open this packet immediately when a Hero target would do more than 12 damage in a single hit. In each envelope would be a little story card, but several new surprises, like maybe an entirely new deck.

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
I really, really don't want the final expansion to be a Legacy expansion.

I loved Pandemic: Legacy. It's maybe the best game I've ever played. But it's over now. I'm probably never going to play it again. Sentinels, on the other hand, is a game that I play over and over again, and to have the final expansion, the thing we've been building to for years, be something that we can only play a certain number of times, or even just get the most out of a certain number of times, would be deeply disappointing.

That said, the superhero genre is ripe for a Legacy game; heroes and villains change and evolve over the years, new threats appear, et cetera. It's something I've considered trying to design myself, though it's got such a large scope that I'd inevitably mess it up...

EDIT: Fortunately, OblivAeon: Legacy is very unlikely, not least because the idea for this predates Risk: Legacy.

I'm not sure. There are three reasons why superheroes wear "costumes".

 

Suit is source of powers or result of powers (not applicable)

Suit is designed to protect identity (considering she's never worn a mask I doubt it)

Suit is a symbol.

 

I think Parse spent a lot of time just going around and helping people. She could help people because of her abilities so she felt that she needed to, however, I doubt she ever really thought of herself as a superhero. More of a Detective or Analyst who sometimes had to fight. After the events of Progeny though (in which we see her in her normal outfit) she realized she needed to become a hero, a symbol, because things were getting dark and people were getting scared.

 

Think about it, you see some dude in jeans and a hoodie fly down out of the sky to fight a rampaging monster, there might be a part of you wondering whose the bigger threat, after all thats just a guy. You see Superman fly down in his outfit, with his cape flowing in the wind and you know your dealing with someone strong enough to handle this… plus it makes a hero more recognizable in the ensuing chaos if they don't look like everyone else.

Throwing in a quick observation here, Christopher mentions that "If OblivAeon succeeds? Nothing will survive", and when asked if Jansa Vi Dero would survive OblivAeon, responds "No. Nothing will." 

These are two cases where the word "nothing" could easily have been part of the previous sentence, but instead starts a sentence and is thus capitalized. But is this because Christopher just decided to phrase them in such a way, or is he obfuscating the idea of Nothing as a named element/entity?

We already know that Wager Master was created by the wager that nothing would happen, a wager that was lost. Perhaps Nothing is more than just the absence of reality. Perhaps Nothing is in fact, something.
